chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Khālid, from Abī al-Rabīʿ, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who takes land from the dahāqīn and then leases it out for more than what he took it for, while undertaking in it the due of the authority. He said: “There is no harm in it. Indeed, land is not like a hired worker, nor like a house. Indeed, the surplus from a worker and a house is haram.”

key_terms.بِحَظِّ ٱلسُّلْطَانِ: with responsibility for the authority’s due or levy
key_terms.فَيُؤَاجِرُهَا: then he leases it out to another party
key_terms.ٱلدَّهَاقِينِ: landowners or local estate-holders from whom the land is taken
key_terms.ٱلْأَرْضَ: land, specifically agricultural land being leased
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتِ: a house or dwelling under rental arrangement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sublease agricultural land for more than the original lease price in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on subleasing agricultural land for a higher amount than the original lease when the lessee also bears the authority’s imposed dues. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes land from hired labor and residential property, indicating that this type of profit in land leasing is permissible while surplus taken from a worker or a house is haram.
